comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue from semi-custom SoC products depends on the success of customers' end products and the company's ability to secure design wins, with no control over customer marketing efforts, meaning actual revenue may not match expectations.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and AMD disclose that their revenue success is fundamentally dependent on the market acceptance of their licensees' or customers' end products, over which the licensor has no control. Qualcomm states its core licensing business depends on licensees' ability to deliver high-volume products with customer acceptance, noting it has no control over their development, sales, or pricing. Similarly, AMD states its semi-custom SoC revenue depends on those products being incorporated into customer products and the success of those products, explicitly noting it has no control over the marketing efforts of these third parties. The key difference is the business model context: Qualcomm describes this as a licensing dependency where licensees are distinct entities, while AMD describes it within the context of semi-custom design services and SoC sales to specific customers.

sentences.text: Moreover, the success of our core licensing business depends in part on the ability of our licensees to continue to develop, introduce and deliver high-volume products that achieve and sustain customer acceptance.
We do not have control over the product development, sales efforts or pricing of products by our licensees, and our licensees might not be successful in these efforts.
Our revenue from our semi-custom SoC products is dependent upon our semi-custom SoC products being incorporated into customers' products and the success of those products.
Moreover, we have no control over the marketing efforts of these third parties, and we cannot make any assurances that sales of their products will be successful in current or future years.
Consequently, the semi-custom SoC product revenue expected by us may not be fully realized and our operating results may be adversely affected.

comparisons.peer_summary: Failure to successfully integrate VMware or achieve expected benefits, particularly regarding customer acceptance of the transition to a subscription licensing model and simplified product portfolio, could adversely affect revenue, financial results, and stock price. Integration requires significant management attention and may divert focus from other issues.
comparisons.comparison: Qualcomm and Broadcom both highlight risks associated with customer acceptance and the lack of control over how the market receives their products or strategies. Qualcomm faces the risk that its licensees' products may not achieve customer acceptance, over which Qualcomm has no control. Broadcom faces the risk that VMware customers may not accept its business strategy, specifically the transition to a subscription licensing model and simplified portfolio, which could lead to loss of customers and adversely affect financial results. While Qualcomm's risk is about product market fit of licensees' goods, Broadcom's risk is about strategic acceptance of its own business model changes post-merger; both share the theme of external market acceptance dictating success without the company having direct control over the customer's final decision.

sentences.text: Moreover, the success of our core licensing business depends in part on the ability of our licensees to continue to develop, introduce and deliver high-volume products that achieve and sustain customer acceptance.

If VMware customers do not accept our business strategy, including our transition from a perpetual to a subscription licensing model and our simplified product portfolio, the investments we have made or may make to implement our strategy may be of no or limited value, we may lose significant customers, our financial results may be adversely affected and our stock price may suffer.

Achieving these benefits will depend, in part, on our ability to integrate VMware's business successfully and efficiently and VMware customers accepting our business strategy, including our transition from a perpetual to a subscription licensing model and our simplified product portfolio.

peer_results.rationale: No candidate was sufficiently comparable. Intec's candidates focus on competition in new markets (AI, foundry) and general product demand/margin variability, which do not directly address the specific risk of dependency on a licensee's or customer's product success and the associated lack of control over that licensee's/customer's marketing or development, which is the core of Qualcomm's disclosure.

No candidate was sufficiently comparable. Micron's candidates focus on system-level solution development dependencies and price volatility. While they mention dependency on customer purchasing volumes, they do not discuss the risk of a licensee's or partner's product failing to gain customer acceptance in the context of a licensing or design-win model where the company has no control over the partner's marketing efforts, distinguishing them from Qualcomm's specific licensee dependency risk.

No candidate was sufficiently comparable. Nvidia's candidates focus on third-party supplier dependency (manufacturing control) and general success factors like adapting to industry changes and R&D. These do not match the specific topic of relying on a licensee or customer's end-product success for revenue generation while lacking control over that licensee's/customer's sales or marketing efforts.
